notes.meaning: John sees an amazing sign in the sky of a woman dressed in the brightness of the sun, with the moon beneath her feet and a crown of twelve stars. She represents God's faithful people, shining with heavenly beauty and honor. Through this community of faith, the promised Savior was brought into the world.

differ.view: Many dispensational teachers believe the woman specifically represents the nation of Israel, pointing to the sun, moon, and twelve stars in Joseph's dream in Genesis.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching sees the woman as the Virgin Mary, the mother of Jesus, as well as a symbol of the church and Israel.

notes.meaning: The woman cries out in severe pain as she is about to give birth. This labor pain pictures the deep suffering, trials, and earnest longings of God's people as they waited for the promised Deliverer to arrive. God hears his people in their darkest times of waiting.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic tradition holds that Mary gave birth without physical pain, viewing this agony as her spiritual sorrow at the cross when Jesus died.

notes.meaning: A second sign appears in the sky showing a massive red dragon with seven heads, ten horns, and seven royal crowns. The monster is a picture of Satan, whose bright red color shows his murderous cruelty. His heads, horns, and crowns display his vast, arrogant power over worldly rulers.

The dragon drags a third of heaven's stars down to earth with his tail and crouches right in front of the mother to eat her baby the moment it is born. This shows Satan leading many rebellious spirits with him and trying desperately to destroy Jesus, just as King Herod tried to kill the infant Christ. Wicked forces may threaten God's promises, but they can never stop them.

The woman gives birth to a son who will rule all nations with a strong iron rod, and he is suddenly taken up to God and his throne. This child is Jesus Christ, whose entire earthly life, resurrection from death, and return to heaven are shown in one quick scene. Because Jesus is safe in heaven, his royal rule can never be overthrown.

The mother runs away into an empty, lonely wilderness where God has prepared a safe haven to feed and protect her for 1,260 days. This means God's people must endure times of trial and hardship on earth, but the Lord always watches over them. Even in dry places, God provides for those who trust him.

differ.view: Reformed teachers understand the 1,260 days as a symbolic number representing the whole church age between Christ's ascension and his second coming.
Dispensational Christians teach that the 1,260 days are a literal three and a half years during a future time of intense tribulation, when Jewish believers will flee to a hiding place such as Petra.
Older Methodist teaching interpreted these days as a historical span of years during the Middle Ages when the true church found refuge in Europe.

notes.meaning: War suddenly breaks out in heaven between the archangel Michael and his angels on one side, and the dragon and his evil angels on the other. God commands his holy heavenly host to battle against the powers of darkness. The forces of evil cannot escape God's judgment.

The dragon is not strong enough to win the fight, and he and his followers lose their place in heaven forever. Evil always has an inner weakness when confronted by God's truth. Satan's boastful strength quickly fades before the power of the Lord.

The great dragon is thrown down to earth along with all his wicked angels. John explains that he is the ancient serpent who tricked Eve, known as the devil, which means slanderer, and Satan, which means adversary or accuser. His power to trick the nations has met a crushing blow.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars view this passage as using an ancient combat story pattern common in the ancient Near East to describe the cosmic defeat of evil.

notes.meaning: A loud heavenly voice announces that God's salvation, kingdom power, and Christ's royal authority have arrived because the enemy has fallen. Satan used to stand before God day and night accusing believers of their sins, but his charges have now been silenced. Christ's victory completely frees believers from condemnation.

differ.view: Reformed Christians believe Satan was cast down and lost his power to accuse believers when Jesus died on the cross and rose again.
Many dispensationalists place this casting down and silencing of accusations at the midpoint of a future seven-year tribulation.

notes.meaning: Believers conquered the evil one through the sacrificial blood of Jesus, the Lamb of God, and through the message they boldly preached. They loved the Lord more than their earthly comfort and were not afraid to die for their faith. Christ's sacrifice gives his followers courage to stand strong in any trial.

The heavens and everyone living in them are called to celebrate the dragon's defeat, but a warning is given to the earth and the sea. The devil has come down filled with terrible fury because he knows he only has a short time before his final end. Even when evil rages, its days are numbered.

When the dragon realizes he has been thrown down to the earth, he turns his anger against the woman who bore the royal child. Since the devil could not hurt Christ in heaven, he attacks God's people living here on earth. Persecution often comes when the enemy knows he is losing.

The woman receives two wings of a great eagle so she can fly quickly away from the serpent into her safe place in the wilderness. There God cares for her for three and a half times, or years. This image recalls how God carried Israel out of Egypt on eagle wings, showing his tender, miraculous rescue of his church.

Unable to catch the woman, the serpent spits a rushing river of water out of his mouth to sweep her away in a flood. This river represents a sudden flood of lies, false teaching, or hostile attacks meant to wipe out the church. God's enemies use deceit when brute force fails.

The earth comes to the woman's aid by opening up and swallowing the entire river poured out by the dragon. God often uses unexpected earthly events and circumstances to swallow up the plans of the wicked. His creation serves his purpose to protect his people.

Furious that he cannot destroy the mother, the dragon goes off to wage war against the rest of her children. These children are everyday believers who obey God's commandments and hold tightly to the truth about Jesus. Faithful obedience makes believers a target for the enemy, but God stays with them through the fight.

differ.view: Dispensationalists differ on who these other children are; some view them as physical Jewish believers during the end times, while others identify them as Gentile converts who turn to Christ during the tribulation.
